Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Ministerio de Justicia - Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for the negative name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office for the definitive commercial registration of the incorporation deed.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital - LSC): Arts. 12 to 22 (incorporation and formalities), Arts. 23 to 30 (articles of association and registered office), Arts. 102 to 109 (SL minimum capital of EUR 3,000 fully paid-in), Art. 137 (sole administrator) and Arts. 124 to 231 (corporate governance organs).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) submitted electronically through the Registro Mercantil Provincial filing system, evidenced by the registration inscription certificate (certificación de inscripción).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 32 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

Statutory minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 under Article 4.1 LSC, fully subscribed and paid in cash or in-kind at constitution; founders must deposit the capital in a temporary blocked escrow account at a Spanish credit institution and obtain a bank deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) attached to the notarial deed; the blocked funds are released upon commercial registration.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certification under the Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE DB-SI) and RD 513/2017; structural load and occupancy certificate under CTE DB-SE issued by a licensed architect; workplace health and safety clearance under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales and RD 486/1997 covering evacuation routes, emergency lighting, fire extinguishers, and safe workstations.

Paid-in capital rule: Statutory minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 under Article 4.1 LSC, fully subscribed and paid in cash or in-kind at constitution; founders must deposit the capital in a temporary blocked escrow account at a Spanish credit institution and obtain a bank deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) attached to the notarial deed; the blocked funds are released upon commercial registration.

(4) Governance - the Board approves opening corporate payment and escrow accounts and authorises filings with the Commercial Registry, the Tax Agency, and Social Security.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic tax procedures are conducted through the AEAT Electronic Office (Sede Electrónica).

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF during incorporation and applies for confirmation of its definitive NIF with the AEAT, generally through Modelo 036 and the required incorporation documents. The company must register for relevant tax obligations, including Corporate Income Tax and VAT, through Modelo 036 before commencing taxable activities. A VAT number for intra-Community transactions (NIF-IVA) requires registration in the Register of Intra-Community Operators through Modelo 036 and validation in VIES. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment generally applies for a Spanish NIF through the AEAT using Modelo 036 and supporting evidence of legal existence and representation; non-EU entities may be required to appoint a Spanish tax representative for VAT purposes, subject to applicable mutual-assistance arrangements.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF during incorporation and applies for confirmation of its definitive NIF with the AEAT, generally through Modelo 036 and the required incorporation documents. The company must register for relevant tax obligations, including Corporate Income Tax and VAT, through Modelo 036 before commencing taxable activities. A VAT number for intra-Community transactions (NIF-IVA) requires registration in the Register of Intra-Community Operators through Modelo 036 and validation in VIES. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment generally applies for a Spanish NIF through the AEAT using Modelo 036 and supporting evidence of legal existence and representation; non-EU entities may be required to appoint a Spanish tax representative for VAT purposes, subject to applicable mutual-assistance arrangements.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

A Spanish SL is generally a separate taxpayer subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax. Spain has no US-style check-the-box election for an SL to be treated as a partnership. Applicable hybrid-mismatch rules may deny deductions or require inclusion in income in specified cross-border arrangements; these rules do not constitute an elective entity-classification regime.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general domestic turnover threshold: a person carrying out taxable economic activity in Spain is generally required to register for VAT from commencement, subject to statutory exemptions and special regimes. Spain's VAT territory excludes the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla, which have separate indirect-tax regimes.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods from the Spanish VAT territory to destinations outside the EU are generally exempt with the right to deduct input VAT if the statutory export conditions are met and the supplier retains evidence that the goods left the EU. Intra-Community supplies may be exempt with the right to deduct where the customer is a taxable person identified for VAT in another Member State, the goods are transported there, and the supplier satisfies reporting and evidentiary requirements. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: place-of-supply rules determine whether Spanish VAT applies, and statutory exceptions may apply. Immigration, visa, and study-abroad advisory services require transaction-specific analysis of customer status, service characterization, and place of supply.

  • Customs export declaration and MRN, with electronic exit-confirmation evidence where available
  • Commercial invoice and transport evidence, such as a bill of lading, airway bill, or carrier confirmation
  • Evidence linking the goods and transport documents to the relevant sale and export transaction
  • Customer VAT identification number and proof of dispatch or arrival in another Member State for an intra-Community supply, where applicable
  • Bank remittance or payment evidence where relevant to substantiate the transaction; an inward remittance certificate and foreign-exchange repatriation are not general Spanish VAT zero-rating requirements

Spain does not generally require real-time AEAT clearance of every invoice. The Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system requires specified taxpayers, including businesses exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04 in annual turnover, VAT groups, and taxpayers registered in the monthly refund regime, to transmit invoice-record data electronically, generally within four calendar days subject to statutory exceptions. Certified invoicing-system and electronic-invoicing obligations are subject to applicable implementing rules and transition dates; the general B2B e-invoicing mandate under the Crea y Crece Law is not a universal real-time clearance system.

Spain imposes no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Unsupported or improperly claimed VAT exemptions can be reversed through assessment, with recovery of underpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and tax penalties under the General Tax Law. Penalty exposure depends on the conduct and culpability; concealment, false documentation, or other aggravating factors can increase sanctions. Input VAT deductions or refunds attributable to ineligible transactions may also be denied or reclaimed.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain applies full euro (EUR) convertibility under Article 63 TFEU. Current-account items are completely liberalized; capital-account transactions (equity, loans, real estate) require only prior statistical declaration (declaración estadística) to the Banco de España via Balance of Payments (BE) forms, not prior authorization. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are unrestricted but attract 19% withholding tax on dividends and interest (24% on royalties) unless reduced by a tax treaty; cash or bearer-note payments above EUR 10,000 are prohibited under Ley 10/2010. For a study-abroad and golden-visa advisory, incoming client and investor funds must match declared commercial contracts, beneficiary registers, and the corporate purpose to avoid re-characterization as undeclared capital income.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No mandatory surrender or conversion requirement exists for export or service proceeds in Spain; receipts may be retained in EUR or any foreign currency. However, every transaction with non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000, and all capital movements regardless of amount when so requested by statistics, must be reported to the Banco de España through BE-22/BE-23 statistical declarations within 15 business days. Failure to file exposes the SL to administrative fines under Law 10/2010 and Banco de España Circular procedures.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting jointly with the Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias (SEPBLAC) for AML supervision and with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation for capital-movement policy.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium to Low. Spanish-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) under Law 21/2011 (PSD2) may provide SEPA-only operational payment accounts, but they cannot legally operate escrow or client-money accounts, which under Spanish banking law are reserved to credit institutions. Non-EEA offshore EMIs cannot onboard a Spanish regulated immigration-visa advisory without a Spanish branch or an EEA passport; UK EMIs lost passporting after Brexit and require re-authorization by the Banco de España. Therefore, all escrow and corporate treasury functions must sit at a Tier-1 Spanish bank.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Sector risk: immigration, study-abroad, and golden-visa advisory with client-money flows routed to third parties (universities, embassies, relocation agents).

Root cause: Sector risk: immigration, study-abroad, and golden-visa advisory with client-money flows routed to third parties (universities, embassies, relocation agents).

Defense evidence: Statutory license file: registration with the Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones where applicable, gestor administrativo or notarial appointment of the compliance officer, the SL board-approved AML/CFT manual, SEPBLAC external auditor report, and itemized client service contracts.
Non-resident, non-EU majority shareholder or director controlling the SL.

Root cause: Non-resident, non-EU majority shareholder or director controlling the SL.

Defense evidence: Tax-residence certificates, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, NIE, notarized board resolutions, apostilled criminal-record certificates (certificado de antecedentes penales) from the country of residence, and 24-month source-of-wealth bank statements.
Client monies deposited into a general operational account without escrow segregation.

Root cause: Client monies deposited into a general operational account without escrow segregation.

Defense evidence: A dedicated client-money escrow account titled 'ES_SL Client Money Escrow', bank-executed escrow terms and conditions, weekly client-money ledger and reconciliation reports under Law 5/2015, professional-indemnity insurance certificate, and an annual forensic accountant attestation.
Large or rapid incoming wire transfers from high-risk jurisdictions (LatAm, China, Middle East) funding tuition or golden-visa packages.

Root cause: Large or rapid incoming wire transfers from high-risk jurisdictions (LatAm, China, Middle East) funding tuition or golden-visa packages.

Defense evidence: Original university admission letter or public-authority acceptance, itemized commercial invoice, student/passport identification file, complete know-your-client documentation, SWIFT gpi intermediary-bank trail, and timely BE-22 declaration to the Banco de España.
PEPs, sanctioned-touch beneficiaries, or multi-layered UBO structures in the client portfolio.

Root cause: PEPs, sanctioned-touch beneficiaries, or multi-layered UBO structures in the client portfolio.

Defense evidence: SEPBLAC PEP screening log, EU/OFSI/UN sanctions screening evidence, enhanced due-diligence questionnaire, Libro Registro de Socios UBO extract, and written approval by the SL compliance officer supported by external counsel opinion.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Inbound capital injections are routed as SWIFT MT103 to the SL operational account at a Banco de España-supervised credit institution, using the BE-22 direct-investment classification code '2510 - Capital contributions to non-listed resident companies' with narration 'Aportación al capital social de ES_SL'. The bank requires a notarized capital-increase deed, registration in the Mercantile Registry, the injecting shareholder's NIE, a source-of-funds declaration, and proof of payment of the 1% capital-operation tax (Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados). Trust and corporate investors must additionally provide a chain-of-ownership chart, CRS self-certification, and home-jurisdiction legal opinion. Student and golden-visa escrow deposits are credited using explicit purpose narration 'Escrow - Study Abroad / Golden Visa' with the escrow agreement attached through the corporate banking portal.EUR disbursements flow through SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) within the SEPA zone; non-EUR and SEPA-excluded payments use SWIFT MT103/MT202 with service-purpose code 'S700 - Business services' for balance-of-payments statistics. Payments to universities, embassies, and relocation partners are released only against a valid invoice, admission letter, or signed escrow disbursement instruction. Commercial letters of credit (UCP 600, SWIFT MT700) are reserved for bulk institutional contracts where the counterparty mandates LC terms. All disbursements above EUR 10,000 pass through enhanced transaction monitoring and require a pre-validated beneficiary master file and recurring-payment mandate.Outright EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm FX forwards (1M-12M) with Spanish credit counterparties under ISDA 2002 / CSANon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or low-liquidity LatAm currencies (USD/MXN, USD/CLP, USD/PEN) executed via Banco de España licensed counterpartiesCross-currency swaps (EUR/USD CCS) for term-liquidity matching on capital injectionsFX swaps (spot/forward combinations) for short-term treasury netting and liquidity management

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium to Low. Spanish-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) under Law 21/2011 (PSD2) may provide SEPA-only operational payment accounts, but they cannot legally operate escrow or client-money accounts, which under Spanish banking law are reserved to credit institutions. Non-EEA offshore EMIs cannot onboard a Spanish regulated immigration-visa advisory without a Spanish branch or an EEA passport; UK EMIs lost passporting after Brexit and require re-authorization by the Banco de España. Therefore, all escrow and corporate treasury functions must sit at a Tier-1 Spanish bank.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Statutory deliverableDeadline window Government feeDelinquency sanctions
Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) deposit with the Mercantile Registry, comprising Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Statement of Changes in Equity, and Management Report Accounts must be approved by the shareholders' general meeting within six months of the fiscal year-end and deposited within one month of approval; for a 31 December year-end the deposit is due no later than 31 July, with registry receipt by 30 July in standard practice $150 USD Late deposit is sanctioned by the Institute of Accounting and Auditing (ICAC) with fines from EUR 1,200 to EUR 180,000; after two consecutive years of non-deposit the Mercantile Registry orders cierre registral (closure of the company's file), suspending all further corporate registrations and effectively blocking operational filings
Corporate Income Tax return (Modelo 200) including annual report of taxable income, deductions, tax credits, and final corporate tax payable Filed within six months and 25 days after the end of the tax period; for a 31 December year-end, the filing window is 1-25 July in the following calendar year $0 USD Late filing triggers surcharges of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% of the tax due depending on delay (3, 6, 12, or more than 12 months), statutory late-interest on unpaid amounts, and a fixed administrative penalty of EUR 1,500 per return; persistent non-filing enables AEAT compulsory assessment and embargoes
Annual Economic Activities Census maintenance confirmation (Modelo 036/037) verifying continued activity under the national tariff for professional and immigration advisory services Ongoing obligation rather than a fixed annual filing; any change of activity, registered office, or relevant fiscal data must be submitted within ten calendar days of the event; where data are unchanged no separate annual confirmation is required $0 USD Failure to file or update the census is an administrative infringement punishable by fines of EUR 400 to EUR 1,000 per instance; inaccuracies may also trigger AEAT rebuttal of the IAE exemption for newly formed entities
Legalization (diligenciado) of annual accounting books, members' register, and minutes book in the Mercantile Registry Annual accounting books must be presented for legalization within four months following the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 30 April; corporate books are legalized upon opening and continuously maintained at the registered office $80 USD Accounting books not legalized lose evidentiary value of reliability before courts and auditors; the registry may impose sanctions and the company's directors face liability for deficient corporate record-keeping under the Capital Companies Act
Annual related-party transaction statement (Modelo 232) disclosing operations with shareholders, directors, and related entities where the amounts exceed EUR 100,000 or represent more than 1% of net equity Filing window identical to Modelo 200: by 25 July following a 31 December fiscal year-end $0 USD Omission or inaccuracy constitutes a tax reporting infringement subject to fixed sanctions of EUR 300 per data record with a EUR 1,500 minimum per return; deliberate failure may be recharacterized as a serious tax offense with penalties up to 50% of the undetected tax base
Annual return deadline

Accounts must be approved by the shareholders' general meeting within six months of the fiscal year-end and deposited within one month of approval; for a 31 December year-end the deposit is due no later than 31 July, with registry receipt by 30 July in standard practice

Statutory government annual fee

$150 USD

Late filing penalties

Late deposit is sanctioned by the Institute of Accounting and Auditing (ICAC) with fines from EUR 1,200 to EUR 180,000; after two consecutive years of non-deposit the Mercantile Registry orders cierre registral (closure of the company's file), suspending all further corporate registrations and effectively blocking operational filings

Strike-off trigger

Mandatory Audit Threshold Mandatory Audit for All Entities

Turnover: An independent statutory audit is compulsory when the SL meets at least two of the following three conditions on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: total assets exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net annual turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees exceeding 50. Audit is also mandatory for entities with listed securities, public-interest entities, and members of a group required to present consolidated accounts; an audit may also be required by shareholders representing 5% of capital.

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to exemptions, treaties, beneficial-ownership requirements, and anti-abuse rules.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

The return is due within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the normal deadline is 25 July of the following year. If the deadline falls on a non-business day, the applicable electronic filing rules extend it to the next business day.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Installment payments are generally made during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. The applicable calculation method is normally based on the prior year's tax liability or, where elected or mandatory for qualifying large taxpayers, on the current-period accounting tax base.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally filed during the eleventh month following the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing period is 1 to 30 November of the following year.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File documentation is generally required for related-party transactions unless a statutory exemption applies. A commonly relevant exemption applies where the aggregate amount of transactions with the same related person or entity does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's-length value during the tax period, subject to transaction-type and anti-abuse limitations. Master File documentation is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to groups with consolidated net turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to statutory content and exemption rules. The EUR 250,000 threshold is not a general exemption from arm's-length pricing, accounting support, or the ability of AEAT to request documentation.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a separate United Arab Emirates-style or Cayman-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime. Economic substance is nevertheless material under Spanish transfer-pricing rules, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, the conflict-in-application-of-tax-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership principles, the controlled foreign company regime, interest and royalty exemptions, treaty anti-abuse provisions, and the principal-purpose and anti-abuse standards applicable to EU and treaty relief. The Spanish SL should maintain genuine local functions, personnel or outsourced operational capacity under its control, premises or adequate operating infrastructure, decision-making, commercial risk assumption, customer contracts, bank-account control, and contemporaneous business records. A conduit company receiving funds and immediately remitting them to a foreign group member is at high risk of denied deductions, recharacterization, withholding-tax assessment, and penalty exposure.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting

Statutory sanction: Tax deficiencies may attract penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, together with late-payment interest and collection costs. Serious tax fraud may constitute a criminal offense where statutory monetary thresholds and intent requirements are met, with fines and imprisonment under the Spanish Criminal Code.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may face subsidiary liability for unpaid tax, civil restitution, disqualification from managing companies, and criminal liability. Travel restrictions or precautionary asset measures are not automatic but may be ordered in criminal or enforcement proceedings. Imprisonment is possible for qualifying tax crimes.
False immigration, visa, or residence documentation

Statutory sanction: Potential offenses include document forgery, fraud, false representation, and offenses against foreign nationals. Sanctions may include administrative fines, loss of authorization, cancellation of applications, civil damages, and criminal imprisonment depending on the conduct and evidence.

Director personal liability: Directors, employees, and agents who knowingly participate may incur direct criminal and civil liability. The limited-liability status of the SL does not protect individuals from personal liability for their own fraudulent acts.
Unlicensed or unauthorized regulated activity

Statutory sanction: Possible administrative fines, prohibition orders, invalidation of filings, consumer claims, professional disciplinary measures, and criminal exposure where unauthorized practice is combined with fraud or document offenses. The exact sanction depends on the activity, autonomous-community rules, and the authority involved.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil damages, administrative disqualification, and criminal liability for knowing authorization breaches or fraudulent representation. Liability is not automatically eliminated by outsourcing work to contractors.
VAT and invoice fraud

Statutory sanction: Assessment of unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and penalties commonly calculated as a percentage of the improperly unpaid, credited, or refunded tax. Serious or repeated fraudulent conduct may result in criminal tax proceedings.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur subsidiary tax liability for deliberately or negligently caused unpaid VAT and may face criminal exposure where the conduct satisfies tax-crime requirements.
Transfer-pricing manipulation and profit shifting

Statutory sanction: AEAT may adjust the Spanish tax base, deny deductions, recharacterize payments, impose withholding tax, require interest, and impose transfer-pricing documentation or valuation penalties. Repeated or intentional concealment may trigger broader tax-evasion sanctions.

Director personal liability: Directors may face subsidiary tax liability and, in deliberate fraud cases, criminal exposure. Personal liability is more likely where directors approved unsupported invoices, concealed beneficial ownership, or ignored professional advice and statutory records.
Shell company, conduit financing, or treaty abuse

Statutory sanction: Denial of treaty or EU directive relief, withholding-tax assessment, denial of expense deductions, recharacterization of transactions, interest, anti-abuse penalties, and potential criminal consequences where concealment or fraud is established.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil restitution, subsidiary tax liability, asset-securing measures, management disqualification, and criminal liability where they knowingly operated the structure as a conduit or sham.
Anti-money laundering and terrorist-financing failures

Statutory sanction: Where the business is an obliged entity under Spanish Law 10/2010, failures may result in administrative sanctions including significant fines, public statements, temporary or permanent prohibitions, and management sanctions. Criminal money-laundering liability may include fines and imprisonment.

Director personal liability: Directors and compliance officers may face personal administrative and criminal liability for knowing participation, grossly negligent controls, concealment, or obstruction. Account freezes and travel restrictions may be imposed by competent authorities in relevant proceedings.
Customer-money misappropriation and escrow misuse

Statutory sanction: Potential breach of contract, consumer-protection rules, fraud, misappropriation, or insolvency-related offenses; consequences may include restitution, damages, account freezing, administrative fines, and criminal penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for unlawful diversion of entrusted funds, including civil restitution and criminal sanctions. Limited liability does not protect intentional misappropriation.
Employment, payroll, and social-security evasion

Statutory sanction: Back payments of social-security contributions, employment-law fines, surcharge and interest, repayment of improperly obtained benefits, and possible criminal liability for serious contribution fraud or illegal employment practices.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur subsidiary liability for unpaid social-security amounts and direct criminal liability for deliberate fraud, exploitation, or illegal-worker arrangements.
Accounting, corporate-record, and beneficial-owner falsification

Statutory sanction: Possible accounting, corporate, tax, insolvency, and criminal sanctions, including financial penalties, director disqualification, rejection of tax deductions, and imprisonment for qualifying offenses.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil liability for creditor and shareholder losses, insolvency liability, disqualification, personal fines, and imprisonment where falsification or fraud is proven.
Data-protection and client-document misuse

Statutory sanction: GDPR and Spanish data-protection sanctions may include orders to stop processing, delete data, notify affected persons, and administrative fines up to the applicable GDPR maximums, subject to the infringement category and the controller's circumstances.

Director personal liability: The company is normally the primary regulated entity, but directors and managers may face civil, employment, or criminal liability for intentional misuse, obstruction, destruction of evidence, or unauthorized disclosure.
Corruption, bribery, and improper payments

Statutory sanction: Criminal fines, confiscation, procurement exclusions, corporate penalties, dissolution or judicial intervention in severe cases, and imprisonment for responsible individuals may apply under Spanish anti-corruption law.

Director personal liability: Directors and employees may face direct criminal liability, civil restitution, asset confiscation, management disqualification, and possible travel restrictions during proceedings.
